findings.title: Opening exclusive restriction
findings.claim: The opening mā closes the scope around the speaker's completed saying, so the reply begins as an exhaustive denial before its authorized content appears.
findings.mechanism: The opening mā carrier at 5:117:1:1 governs the perfect qultu and meets illā at 5:117:4:1; that contact confines the speech record before the exception names what was permitted.
findings.reader_payoff: The ayah first presents a bounded defense whose permitted content is still to be specified.
findings.containment: The ordinary local grammatical reading remains recoverable. This finding adds the supplied form, relation, lexical, sound, or boundary pressure within 5:117 and does not make a surah-wide claim.

findings.title: Accountable speech record
findings.claim: The first-person perfect qultu turns the question into a record of what the speaker said to the group and places his own speech under examination.
findings.mechanism: The qultu carrier at 5:117:2:1 meets the opening negator and the following command relation; its perfect first-person form makes the utterance a completed, accountable speech event.
findings.reader_payoff: The reply is heard as testimony about a completed act of speaking, not as an unframed teaching summary.

findings.title: Community-directed worship
findings.claim: The plural imperative uʿbudū makes worship of Allah the direct command delivered to the whole recipient group.
